captive_summary: Viva Energy's proposed 3 mtpa FSRU import terminal next to its Geelong refinery (announced Dec 2020, pre-FID/proposed as of GEM's current record). The EES Executive Summary (now retrieved and read in full) documents that the FSRU's REGASIFICATION process can use 'gas-fired boilers' in closed-loop mode to reheat seawater — an explicitly thermal/heating application, not electricity generation, and one the EES itself frames as the less-preferred, higher-emission mode versus the default open-loop (seawater-only, no gas combustion) mode. The document does not address the FSRU vessel's own electrical/hotel-load power supply (onboard dual-fuel generators vs. shore power), which is the actual captive-power question under the SOP's FSRU convention.
confirmed_how: Recovery pass: retrieved and pdftotext-extracted the Viva Energy Gas Terminal Project EES Executive Summary in full (vivaenergy.com.au/ArticleDocuments/1193/VE-EES-EXCSUM_WEB.pdf.aspx, ~1900 lines) and searched it for power/generation/engine/turbine/electric/Hoegh terms. Findings: (1) Section 2.2.1 'FSRU operation' describes three regasification modes — open loop (seawater as heating medium, no gas combustion, 'the usual operating mode'), closed loop ('gas-fired boilers' reheat recirculated water), and combined loop; (2) the GHG section (4.2.2) states 'Fuel consumed by the FSRU would be the primary source of greenhouse gas emissions' during operation (Scope 1), while 'electricity consumed at Refinery Pier and within the treatment facility' is separately categorised as Scope 2 (imported grid electricity) — i.e., the plant's own gas combustion (the boilers) is explicitly the Scope-1 finding, and imported/grid electricity is a SEPARATE, distinct line item for the pier/treatment-facility infrastructure. This establishes the boilers are a thermal (regasification-heat) application under the SOP's 'power, not heat' rule, not captive power — but the document never states whether the FSRU vessel's own hotel-load/auxiliary electrical demand is met by onboard generators (which would be the real captive-power question per the FSRU convention) or by shore power/cold-ironing from the refinery. This is a materially different, more precise finding than the primary pass's total access failure (403 on every host), but it does not resolve the actual question either way.
